reuse.why: Reuses findOrCreateBank, syncAccount, handleSyncResponse and adds one shared guard called by every link handler, but the unlink-on-replace re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset instead of reusing it and the Fintegra link/download are near-verbatim copies of the Pluggy ones.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount copies linkPluggyAiAccount almost line for line, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadPluggyAiTransactions, and the replacement path copies unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount reset block; the helper also repeats the link handlers' 'account not found' lookup.

placement.why: Guard lives in accounts/app.ts next to the link handlers, download in sync.ts, server URL in server-config and type in types/models, matching the tree's layering; only the guard mutating other accounts is a slightly odd place for unlinking.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the four requested behaviours plus required wiring (provider list, client label/flag, release notes); the client edits are minimal type-satisfying additions.

maintainability.why: One guard enforces the rules for all providers, which is good, but it is named as an assertion while it also unlinks accounts, and each new provider still means another ~70-line copy of link and download code.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in accounts/app.ts unlinks the previous holder with its own db.updateAccount field reset instead of going through the existing unlinkAccount logic (whose reset fields it duplicates).

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra link handler vs Pluggy, Fintegra download vs Pluggy download, unlink field reset vs unlinkAccount) are verbatim, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked grew a replaceExistingLink parameter (step 4) and gained a closed-target branch (step 3) and an unlink-and-proceed branch with its own existence check (step 4), turning an assertion into a mixed validate/mutate helper; all six link handlers call it.
